Topic 11.1: Listening and Speaking 11.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 11.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, part of Play time and games Suggested vocabulary games, break, kick, ankle, kind, find,  in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade three ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to learn new vocabulary? 2. How can we communicate with people apart from using the spoken word?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 11.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: The learner’s ability to speak clearly and effectively is enhanced as they construct sentences about play time

and games using the new words.

• Learning to learn: The learner’s ability to develop relationships is enhanced as they collaboratively practise pronunciation of words with target

letter-sound combinations with peers.

Values:
Respect: Patience is enhanced as the learner takes turn to listen to peers during discussions.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills (Self-esteem): The learner acquires high level of self-esteem as they interpret and respond to instructions appropriately.

Links to other Learning Areas:
The learner applies pronunciation skills to learning of similar concept in Kiswahili and Indigenous Language Activities.

● Print textbooks in appropriate font size and colour contrast

● Braille books

● Digital devices with assistive technology,

● Charts, flash cards or braille cards,

● Pictures or picture description
